item.title: Validity of the Behrens--Fisher solution
item.description: arXiv:2611.06987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Behrens--Fisher fiducial interval for the difference of two normal means is known from the numerical work of Robinson (1976) to be conservative, but a proof has been lacking. The results here prove that the fiducial interval for any linear combination of $k$ normal means has coverage probability at least its nominal level for all values of the unknown variances. Taraldsen (2026) explains this in more detail using the original data of Behrens (1926). The proof presented in the following rests on a novel plug-in inequality: if a threshold function controls a scaled sum of pivots pointwise in the scale vector, then it also controls the sum with the observed scales plugged in, provided the location errors satisfy a concentration condition formulated through a weighted geometric mean. Independent normal errors satisfy the condition.
item.dc:creator: Gunnar Taraldsen

item.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the martingale property of stochastic exponentials driven by multi-dimensional diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2611.07083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give necessary and sufficient coefficient conditions for stochastic exponentials driven by multidimensional diffusions to be true martingales. The classical reduction to non-exit of the diffusion with Girsanov-shifted drift separates the analysis into smooth boundary points, infinity, and nonsmooth boundary pieces. On smooth domains, under regularity and non-explosion hypotheses, martingality is equivalent to nonpositivity of the shifted Fichera drift, provided an explicit local condition holds where that drift vanishes and the stochastic integrand is unbounded. At infinity, Feller's test gives exact criteria when a scalar function of the diffusion reduces to a one-dimensional diffusion up to a time change with rate bounded above and away from zero. General radial and projection tests supply sufficient conditions. Applications give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions for inverse-CIR and $4/2$ models with correlated factors and singular stochastic integrands, including critical equality cases. The coupled non-affine examples go beyond direct scalar Feller tests and affine Riccati criteria, and exhibit boundary exits not decided by tests at infinity. Further exact criteria cover logarithmic boundary singularities, weighted distances, and an absorbed factor. The martingale conditions also yield uniqueness criteria for associated valuation equations.
item.dc:creator: Erhan Bayraktar, Hao Xing

item.title: A second eigenvalue lower bound for the directed configuration model
item.description: arXiv:2611.07104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a high-probability lower bound for the second eigenvalue in modulus of the transition matrix of the simple random walk on a directed configuration model with minimal out-degree at least two and maximal degree not too large. The lower bound matches the upper bound found by Coste (2021) on the same model. Our proof bypasses the need to establish convergence of the empirical eigenvalue distribution. Instead, it reduces the spectral lower bound to a central limit theorem for the trace of the transition matrix at powers much larger than the logarithmic scale, a range that previous results failed to reach. Both the general strategy and the central limit theorem might be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Charles Bordenave, Yizhe Zhu

item.title: Weak uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with nondegenerate diffusion: the full H\"older regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.07310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove weak well-posedness for the scalar stochastic heat equation on the one-dimensional torus with uniformly nondegenerate diffusion that is Holder continuous of any positive order. This resolves the weak uniqueness problem in the full positive Holder range, extending our earlier result for exponents above two thirds (arXiv:2608.01279). The proof couples a weak solution to a smooth companion and uses spatial cancellation to estimate the signed covariance difference in a negative Sobolev norm. A finite Gaussian expansion on each Littlewood-Paley block gives the decay needed to remove the coupling drift by a change of measure. A localized Girsanov argument extends the result to measurable drifts of linear growth.
item.dc:creator: Yi Han

item.title: Approximate independence of typical marginals of high-dimensional probability measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.07460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For many probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and for $k$ sufficiently smaller than $n$, most $k$-dimensional coordinate marginals are close to product measures. We prove this in two regimes, which notably involve no exchangeability assumptions as in prior theorems of de Finetti type. First, for log-concave measures, the quantitative bound depends on the measure only through the operator norm of its correlation matrix, and $k$ may grow polynomially with $n$. A key ingredient of the proof is a new strengthening of the subadditivity of relative entropy for strongly log-concave measures, which as a byproduct yields sharp bounds in the strongly log-concave case. Second, for a broad class of measures satisfying just a variance inequality much weaker than Poincar\'e's, $k$ must stay below the sharp threshold $2\log n/\log \log n$. Here the basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is fixed a priori, which makes this phenomenon quite different from known Gaussian approximations for low-dimensional projections such as the central limit theorem for convex bodies, although there are remarkable parallels. Insofar as Gaussian approximations are driven by the thin shell property, our results are driven by variance inequalities for additive functions which have appeared in the literature on the Gibbs sampler.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Arnese, Daniel Lacker

item.title: Nonlinear optimal stopping and domineering claims
item.description: arXiv:2611.07743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study nonlinear optimal stopping and domineering claims in a Brownian--Poisson filtration, under a nonlinear evaluation induced by a Lipschitz BSDE driver satisfying a comparison condition. A nonlinear domineering claim is a strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-martingale dominating the reward process at every stopping time. We first establish the existence of such claims for every optional reward in $\mathcal{S}^2$. For left-limited, right-upper semicontinuous rewards, we prove a local dual representation at every stopping time: the nonlinear optimal stopping value equals the essential infimum of the values of all domineering claims defined on the remaining stochastic interval. This infimum is attained by a claim constructed from the associated reflected BSDE. We further show that a global domineering claim attains the value at a prescribed stopping time if and only if the reflection processes have accumulated no increase up to that time, with the appropriate endpoint convention. When the reward is right-upper semicontinuous in $\mathcal{E}^f$-expectation and the family of contact times is nonempty, its essential infimum is optimal. Under strict comparison, we also establish a necessary contact condition for optimality. No convexity assumption on the driver is required.
item.dc:creator: Siham Bouhadou, Oussama Lamhadoul, Youssef Ouknine

item.title: Geometric Functional Inequalities for Markov Processes: An Invitation via the Langevin Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.07785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Functional inequalities provide a language for reasoning about the long-time properties of ergodic Markov processes in terms of their macroscopic geometry. This article offers an informal introduction to functional inequalities for readers who are more familiar with probabilistic tools based around couplings, Lyapunov techniques, and similar. The main ideas are developed through the overdamped Langevin diffusion, where various functionals related to this convergence admit particularly transparent expressions, and for which the key associated inequalities -- namely, the Poincar\'{e} and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities -- are especially well-studied. We explain the qualitative content of these inequalities, what they imply about convergence to equilibrium, how they transform and compose under natural operations, and how they interface with classical probabilistic approaches. Related inequalities are discussed more briefly, and an annotated guide is provided for readers wishing to enter the wider literature.
item.dc:creator: Sam Power

item.title: Recurrence and Uniqueness Criteria for Markov Processes from Moments of Integral-Type Functionals
item.description: arXiv:2611.07821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate recurrence and uniqueness of continuous-time Markov chains using moments of integral-type functionals. Unlike the classical criteria from Chen (2004) and the Feller-Reuter criterion, we develop general unified conditions for recurrence and uniqueness of Markov processes based on moments of integral-type functionals. The associated criteria follow directly from these conditions whenever the mean functionals can be expressed explicitly. As applications, explicit recurrence and uniqueness criteria are derived for single-birth, single-death, and birth-death processes on trees.
item.dc:creator: Ling-Di Wang, Yu-Hui Zhang, Zu-Yi Zhao

item.title: A Feynman-Kac Representation and Large Deviation Bounds for the Fisher-KPP Equation Driven by Finite-Activity Pure Jump Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.07868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic propagation speed of travelling wave solutions to the stochastic Fisher-KPP equation with multiplicative finite-activity pure jump L\'evy noise. The noise is represented by a compensated Poisson random measure with finite intensity, so that the solution evolves deterministically between successive jump times and undergoes multiplicative jumps at the event times. Our main contribution is a stochastic Feynman-Kac representation for the solution, which expresses the random field as the product of the exponential martingale of the jump noise and an expectation over the paths of an independent Brownian motion. This representation is the key probabilistic tool that converts the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation into an expectation problem, thereby allowing for a direct analysis of the front position. Building on this representation and on the large deviation analysis of the jump noise, we derive explicit upper and lower bounds for the asymptotic wave speed. These bounds are given in terms of the noise intensity $\epsilon$ and the L\'evy measure $\mu$, providing a quantitative description of how discontinuous stochastic forcing affects the propagation speed in the Fisher-KPP equation. Under the finite-activity assumption, a stopping-time iteration yields pathwise $L^\infty$ bounds and finite-speed propagation of the level sets of the front, which are essential for establishing the existence of a travelling wave profile. The framework extends naturally to multi-species cooperative systems, illustrating its robustness. Numerical simulations are included to demonstrate the informativeness of the theoretical speed bounds.
item.dc:creator: Yuhong Li, Hao Wen, Jianhua Huang

item.title: The second reconstruction transition for random graphs from 2-neighborhoods
item.description: arXiv:2611.07890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, with high probability, the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph $G(n,p)$ is reconstructible up to isomorphism from the multiset of its rooted induced 2-neighborhoods whenever $p\geq n^{-3/4}(\log n)^3$. Together with the non-reconstructibility result of Johnston, Kronenberg, Roberts and Scott, our result locates the second reconstruction transition at the scale $p=n^{-3/4}$ up to polylogarithmic factors, resolving a question they posed. Our proof relies on a global rigidity argument exploiting 5-cycle constraints.
item.dc:creator: Yiming Chen

item.title: Constructive Probability, Foundations and Numerical Analysis for mathematical finance and machine learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.07944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This monograph sets out a constructive theory of stochastic processes in the continuum, in the sense of constructive field theory: the continuum is not postulated but reached as the limit of a sequence of lattice approximations, with the renormalisation the limit requires exhibited rather than assumed, and the limit controlled by estimates that can be checked. The primitive object is not a sigma-algebra but de Finetti's prevision, the price of finitely many gambles at a fixed resolution, which coherence turns into a conditional expectation. The theorem at the centre of the book, called plainly the fundamental theorem, is at once de Finetti's fundamental theorem of probability, the fundamental theorem of Bayesian statistics, and the one-period fundamental theorem of asset pricing; the financial vocabulary is a convenience only. The applications are two, mathematical finance and machine learning, and they are one mathematics read in opposite directions: an assessment is a price in the one and a prediction in the other, and both are computed by one adjoint recursion, the adjoint of a propagation in the first case and backpropagation in the second. Carried through, the two directions give sharp rates of convergence rather than asymptotic orders: for the moments of Ito diffusions, for the value function of Feynman-Kac semigroups, and for the measure changes of the fundamental theorem, the last as a limit theorem for reweighted generators, under a condition keeping the reweighting well behaved. A measure change is thus calculated, not postulated: a lattice approximation with Farkas' lemma computes it, completeness makes it unique, and the passage to the continuum is earned by the regularity of what is computed. Sixty-seven Python scripts regenerate every numerical table, and much of the finite-dimensional core of the argument has been verified in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Claudio Albanese

item.title: The stochastic Ginzburg-Landau equation with harmonic potential in the full subcritical regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.08038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct the complex Ginzburg-Landau dynamic associated with the harmonic oscillator, with a random force which is white in time and covers the full subcritical range in space. We are able to renormalise the non-linearity using the same constant as the one used to renormalise the problem associated to the Laplacian. By an extension of the problem to complex times, we are able to prove that the solution of the complex Ginzburg-Landau is equal in law to the solution of the purely dissipative case, i.e. the associated complex $\Phi^4$ model, but along a complex axis of time.
item.dc:creator: Sama\"el Mackowiak, Aur\'elien Minguella

item.title: On some stochastic evolutions on Laguerre-Polya functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.08073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove uniqueness in law for three stochastic evolutions on normalised Laguerre-P\'{o}lya functions arising as scaling limits of matrix characteristic polynomial dynamics. In particular, this implies that Ahn's universal Brownian Gibbs line ensemble arising from random matrix products has the law of the logarithms of the reciprocal zeros of the solution, unique in law, to a simple stochastic equation on entire functions started from $\mathrm{e}^{-z}$. The method of proof relies on some integrable structure of the problem in the special form of a new duality with finite-dimensional diffusions which is closely related to intertwinings.
item.dc:creator: Theodoros Assiotis, Fengyi Li

item.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the self-normalized central limit theorem for independent triangular arrays
item.description: arXiv:2611.08137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a rowwise independent triangular array $\{X_{n,i}:1\le i\le n\}$, put $S_n=\sum_{i=1}^nX_{n,i}$ and $V_n^2=\sum_{i=1}^nX_{n,i}^2$. We prove that $S_n/V_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}{\mathrm N}(0,1)$ implies $\max_{i\le n}|X_{n,i}|/V_n\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0$. The same assumption gives $V_n^2/b_n^2\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}1$ for any choice of medians $b_n^2$ of $V_n^2$. Combined with the results of Shao (2018), this yields necessary and sufficient conditions for the self-normalized central limit theorem and resolves his conjecture for independent sequences. The proof identifies the joint limits of the sum and its sum of squares, then uses the standard normal ratio to remove every non-Gaussian component.
item.dc:creator: Xiang Li, Song-Hao Liu, Qi-Man Shao, Hao Shi, Jing-Yu Xu

item.title: Existence, Uniqueness, Feller Property and Diricihlet form of the Keller-Segel particle system up to blow up
item.description: arXiv:2611.08207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Keller-Segel particle system as defined in \cite{ft} through the Dirichlet form theory (see \cite{f}) consists of $N$ planar Brownian motions interacting through the kernel $x\in \rr^2 \mapsto \theta K(x) = -\theta x/\|x\|^2$, where $\theta >0$. One particularity of this model is that collisions (i.e. overlapping of particles) occur depending on the value of $\theta$, making the well-posedness of the particle system delicate. In this work, we propose a new notion of solution of this SDE without relying on the Dirichlet form theory and prove uniqueness in law of such solutions. The proof relies on an excursion decomposition of the particle system based on the "barycenter-radius-angle" decomposition in \cite{ft}. As additional results, we prove that the solution is strong Markov, has the Feller property and fits in the definition of solutions in the Dirichlet form sense. Finally we prove that the law of the particle system starting from a configuration where all the particles overlap is explicit.
item.dc:creator: Yoan Tardy

item.title: Ignoring Blow-Ups for Approximations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well known that for SDEs with non-Lipschitz coefficients, the Euler scheme can fail to converge in an Lp sense. It is also widely observed that convergence fails only due to rare explosive trajectories, that distort the expectation. In this work we demonstrate that almost any method of removing these rare explosive trajectories leads to convergence in a suitable strong and weak sense. We apply this framework to coefficients that grow faster than linearly at infinity and Lennard-Jones type coefficients that explode like a reciprocal power on a compact set.
item.dc:creator: Tim Johnston

item.title: Random Fibonacci Tilings
item.description: arXiv:2611.08317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Fibonacci spiral is formed by a square-joining rule: begin with a unit square and attach squares whose side lengths follow the Fibonacci sequence; in the standard construction, choices of direction produce a spiral and a tiling of the plane. We study a randomization of this construction, in which the attachment axis alternates deterministically, while fair coin flips determine direction. For a lattice point we ask when the growing rectangle first covers that point and how the expected covering time depends on its location. Tracking the rectangle's boundary reduces this question to random subset sums of even- and odd-indexed Fibonacci numbers. We extend the construction to d dimensions, where coordinate subsequences are super-increasing, allowing us to derive exact covering probabilities and formulas for the expectation and variance. For $d\geq2$, the expected covering time grows logarithmically with distance from the initial block, while the variance remains uniformly bounded. We obtain exponential tail bounds for the delay beyond the earliest feasible covering stage. Finally, we extend the Fibonacci spiral to the randomized tiling through a square-by-square construction using circular arcs and quintic connectors. This construction uses one-step lookahead, admits a continuously differentiable parameterization, and recovers the Fibonacci spiral for the standard tiling.
item.dc:creator: Yuval Amit, Azmera Gebre, Christopher Housholder, Joshua Khan, Steven Miller, Emily Upton, Connor Yau

item.title: Fluctuations, Moderate and Large Deviations about Hydrodynamic Limits of Space-Time Hawkes Processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Gaussian fluctuations, moderate and large deviations around the high-density hydrodynamic limit of critical and nearly critical space-time Hawkes processes initialized by a prescribed Poisson field of past events, with no subsequent immigration. Under a finite mean reproduction delay and centered displacements with finite spatial covariance, a positive cluster-transform estimate yields a distribution-valued central limit theorem (CLT) and a moderate deviation principle (MDP) throughout the moderate range. For finite nonzero mass of the initial profile, we obtain a full large deviation principle (LDP) for the space-time event measure in the vague topology; its good rate function is a quadratic branching-control energy with a prescribed initial trace and a finite-mass domain. The lower bound uses an explicit approximation by smooth reproduction controls, and the upper bound uses a microscopic exponential martingale and a global generator approximation. We distinguish exact-mean centering from PDE centering and compute deterministic bias corrections under second delay and fourth spatial moments. For a factorized heavy-tail power-law delay, we establish the CLT, MDP, and full measure-valued LDP for the space-time measure, with finite nonzero mass of the initial profile for the LDP. Its fractional control energy retains the source generated by the prescribed past. A source-preserving regularization proves approximation of every finite-action measure. Compact-kernel bounds for initial profiles of infinite mass and the degenerate case of a zero initial profile are stated separately.
item.dc:creator: Fuqing Gao, Yingli Wang, Lingjiong Zhu

item.title: Global solutions for continuous-time Burgers equations and infinite-volume polymer measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.08355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stochastic Burgers equation on the whole space, driven by space-homogeneous Gaussian noises that are white in time and colored in space, for both positive and zero viscosity. We show that in dimension one, for any fixed average velocity, there is a unique ergodic global solution to the Burgers equation for all nonnegative viscosities, and that the One Force---One Solution principle holds. We also describe the basin of attraction and show that these global solutions are one-point pullback attractors. Moreover, the viscous global solution converges to the inviscid global solution as the viscosity tends to zero. Our technique relies on the study of polymer measures; accordingly, we establish the existence and uniqueness of infinite-volume polymer measures in a given asymptotic direction, as well as their convergence to semi-infinite minimizers in the zero-temperature limit. We also establish the existence part of all these results in arbitrary dimension larger than one.
item.dc:creator: Liying Li

item.title: The singular Gaussian scaling limit for a tagged particle in the infinite-dimensional Dyson model at $\beta=2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.08365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a logarithmic central limit theorem for a tagged particle in infinite-dimensional Dyson Brownian motion at inverse temperature $\beta=2$, starting from the sine$_2$ point process. The fluctuation is of order $\sqrt{\log t}$, which is subdiffusive and substantially slower than the polynomial fluctuations of classical short-range interacting particle systems, reflecting the rigidity induced by long-range logarithmic repulsion. We further identify the scaling limit as the singular Gaussian field corresponding to the zero-Hurst parameter, which provides a realisation of the singular Gaussian field as a scaling limit of a tagged particle raised by D\"urr, Goldstein and Lebowitz (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 38 (1985)).
item.dc:creator: Hirofumi Osada, Kohei Suzuki

item.title: A Simple Approach to the Complexity of Mean Field Ising Spin Glasses
item.description: arXiv:2611.08374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The geometry of spherical spin glasses is relatively well understood, thanks in large part to the Kac-Rice formula. However, this formula does not directly apply to discrete spin systems, and much less is known mathematically about the geometry of Ising spin glasses. In this paper, we present a simple method for counting local optima and gapped states in a broad class of discrete spin glasses. To illustrate its scope, we compute the annealed complexities ("configurational entropies," in the physics language) of mixed Ising spin glasses with potentials, such as external fields, and of the Ghatak-Sherrington model. These computations recover several existing results in the mathematics and physics literature as special cases. We can also compute energy-constrained complexity, finding a critical energy threshold analogous to the spherical case, but for gapped states of pure Ising spin glasses. Finally, we use our method to establish a form of disorder persistence for gapped states, identifying a transition between $3$-spin and $4$-spin glasses.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin McKenna, Qiang Wu

item.title: A Central Limit Theorem For Random Variables Under A Constraint
item.description: arXiv:2611.08446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider vectors chosen randomly from high-dimensional hypersurfaces of the form $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n: \sum_{j=1}^n V_j(x_j)=an\}$. These in general asymmetric surfaces generalize classical spheres and include unbounded and disconnected surfaces. We show that under mild assumptions as $n\to\infty$, any weighted sum of the random coordinates is asymptotically Gaussian, provided that no weight dominates. An explicit reduction in the variance compared to the unconstrained case is observed. We also study a model with penalization of deviations from the constraint, interpolating between the unconstrained and the constrained case. Our approach involves an explicit representation of the characteristic function of the constrained random variables in terms of independent random variables.
item.dc:creator: Jack Cromwell, Martin Venker

item.title: Almost sure bounds and tail phases for critical non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
item.description: arXiv:2611.08467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gu and Zhang asked for almost sure upper and lower bounds on the Taylor coefficients $a_n$ of $\exp(\sum_{k\ge1}X_kz^k/\sqrt{k})$ in the unit disc, and for the dependence of these bounds on the input tail. For independent, identically distributed, rotationally invariant complex inputs with $\mathbb E|X_1|^2=1$, we prove the universal almost sure bound $|a_n|=O((\log n)^{1/4})$. Almost surely, $\limsup_{n\to\infty}|a_n|/(\log n)^{1/4}$ is positive and finite exactly when $\mathbb E[|X_1|^2\log^+|X_1|^2]<\infty$, and is zero otherwise. For each input law, we define a deterministic scale such that, almost surely, the coefficients are bounded exactly when the scale is bounded, and tend to zero exactly when it vanishes. We also determine the almost sure logarithmic growth exponent as the maximum of contributions from collective fluctuations and individual large inputs. Explicit tails exhibit distinct thresholds for boundedness and for upper bounds at the scale in the phase criteria. Examples show that neither the leading tail nor the set of finite logarithmic moments determines the almost sure phase.
item.dc:creator: Feng Guo

item.title: Approximating the Euclidean Ball by Polytopes: Surprising Rates in High Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34651v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide sharp estimates on the number of vertices needed to approximate the Euclidean unit ball $B_d\subset\mathbb R^d$ with relative symmetric-difference volume error at most $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$. We show that the minimum vertex budget $N_\varepsilon(d)$ satisfies $$\log N_\varepsilon(d)\asymp d\log\left(1+\frac1{\varepsilon\sqrt d}\right).$$ In particular, $\exp(O(\sqrt d/\varepsilon))$ vertices suffice for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and all sufficiently large $d$. We also prove that achieving a fixed error $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ requires at least $\Omega\bigl((\tfrac{1+\varepsilon}{2\sqrt\varepsilon})^{d-1}\bigr)$ facets, an exponential number in $d$. We extend our vertex approximation result to Gaussian symmetric-difference error, and give a positive answer to the question of De, Nadimpalli, and Servedio about subexponential vertex complexity for approximating Euclidean balls. We also disprove a Macbeath-type extremality principle for unrestricted vertex approximation. Whereas the ball uniformly maximizes the inscribed approximation error among all convex bodies (Macbeath, 1951), we show that approximating the hypercube $[-1,1]^d$ to relative error $\varepsilon$, with $\delta:=1-\varepsilon$, requires $N\ge\frac{\delta}{2}\exp(\Omega(\delta^2d/\log^2(2/\delta)))$ vertices whenever $d\ge16\log(2/\delta)$. Thus, when $d$ is large, the cube is harder to approximate than the ball in this sense. Finally, we determine the sharp dimensional order of the classical Laguerre-Delone triangulation number, showing that $\mathrm{ldel}_{d-1}=\Theta(d^{-1/2})$ as $d\to\infty$. This improves both the upper bound of Ludwig, Sch\"utt, and Werner and the lower bound of B\"or\"oczky by a factor of order $\sqrt d$. By classical asymptotic approximation theorems (Ludwig, 1999), this improvement applies to every convex body in $\mathbb R^d$ with $C^2$ boundary and positive Gaussian curvature.
item.dc:creator: Yegor Gorodzha, Steven Hoehner, Gil Kur

item.title: An Obukhov-Corrsin-Yaglom law for a kinematic model of turbulence
item.description: arXiv:2611.07076v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove an Obukhov-Corrsin-Yaglom-type law for passive scalars advected by a family of random $C^\alpha$ velocity field proposed in \cite{JDEMS} as a kinematic model of turbulent fluids. Up to a technical assumption on one parameter, the expectation of the squared $L^2_t H^\gamma_x$ norm of solutions to the passive scalar equation is bounded by the squared $L^2$ norm of the deterministic initial datum, uniformly in the viscosity, whenever $\alpha + 2\gamma < 1$. The proof is based on a new insight in the theory developed by \cite{FM} to prove Richardson's dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the same model.
item.dc:creator: Camillo De Lellis

item.title: A Survey of Nonlinear Filtering Methods for Data Assimilation and Recent Advances in Generative AI-Enabled Score Filters
item.description: arXiv:2611.07160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many real-world applications, such as numerical weather prediction or wildfire tracking, involve modeling highly nonlinear dynamical systems that are chaotic and influenced by various sources of uncertainty. To improve model prediction accuracy and reduce such uncertainties, data assimilation (DA) combines the dynamical model with partial, noisy observations to estimate the evolution of the system's state. Doing so depends on solving the optimal filtering problem: computing the conditional distribution of a hidden state given a sequence of observations. Classical approaches fail along three distinct axes: Kalman-based methods assume Gaussian posteriors and produce biased estimates under nonlinear observation operators; particle-based methods represent distributions with weighted samples and collapse in high dimensions due to the curse of dimensionality; and kernel-based methods move beyond discrete particle representations but cannot maintain their density approximation affordably as dimension grows. The Ensemble Score Filter (EnSF) avoids all three constraints by encoding the filtering density in a score function and approximating that score with a training-free Monte Carlo estimator, enabling stable filtering in high-dimensional, chaotic systems. This survey traces EnSF's mathematical foundations, establishes it as the state of the art for non-Gaussian, high-dimensional filtering, and examines fourteen extensions that expand its operational reach. Twelve of the fourteen extensions preserve this training-free Monte Carlo estimator at the core of the update, with only two departing from it to achieve planetary-scale deployment.
item.dc:creator: Cath Pham, Kadesha Reynolds

item.title: Multiplayer Stopping Games with a Conditionally Atomless Filtration
item.description: arXiv:2611.07184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stopping games are the multiplayer generalization of optimal stopping problems, in which each player independently chooses when to stop, and the payoff depends on who stops first and when. While the existence of $\varepsilon$-equilibria in two-player stopping games with integrable payoffs is known, the multiplayer case has remained open. We prove that every multiplayer stopping game in discrete time with integrable payoff process admits an $\varepsilon$-equilibrium for every $\varepsilon > 0$, provided the filtration is conditionally atomless. This condition is satisfied, in particular, when the underlying probability space is $\{0,1\}^{\dN}$ endowed with the uniform measure and its natural filtration. Our method also shows that every three-player stopping game, without the restriction to conditionally atomless filtration, admits an $\varepsilon$-equilibrium, for every $\varepsilon > 0$. The proof combines techniques developed for two-player stopping games and for multiplayer quitting games, with a key new insight: the richness encoded in a conditionally atomless filtration can substitute for an external public randomization device, allowing players to coordinate without an explicit coordination signal.
item.dc:creator: Robert Samuel Simon, Eilon Solan, Grzegorz Tomkowicz

item.title: On the critical value of void percolation in high dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.07196v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the random Lorentz gas, a point tracer moves through spherical obstacles of (reduced) density $\Phi$ centered on a Poisson point process in $d$-dimensional space, $\mathbb{R}^d$, and becomes localized once the vacant space stops percolating, at $\Phi_{\rm p}(d)$. The dimensional scaling of this void percolation threshold has remained elusive. Prior bounds, conjectural ones included, ranged from $\Omega(1)$ to $O(d\ln d)$, leaving even the scaling undetermined. We here prove that $\Phi_{\rm p}(d)=\Theta(d)$, and in particular that $\tfrac12\,d \le \Phi_{\rm p}(d) \le 5\,d$ for all sufficiently large $d$. The upper bound counts hierarchical families of escape waypoints called tree embeddings; the lower bound is via a weighted second-moment estimate on an explicit ensemble of ballistic escape routes. A linear scaling of $\Phi_{\rm p}(d)$ excludes the $d\ln d$ growth suggested by analogy with other systems in the random first-order transition universality class and is consistent with the numerical estimate $\Phi_{\rm p}/d \to 3.40(5)$. Because the mean-field dynamical transition is likewise linear, $\Phi_{\rm d}\simeq 2.40\,d$, our result fixes the activated window $[\Phi_{\rm d},\Phi_{\rm p}]$ as a bounded---rather than diverging---correction to mean-field dynamical arrest in sufficiently high $d$.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Charbonneau, Marcus Michelen

item.title: Random complex cross ratios
item.description: arXiv:2611.07670v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the cross ratio of four independent points chosen uniformly on the Riemann sphere. A positive integral over a two-dimensional simplex gives its normalized planar density. We then evaluate this integral in terms of the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm, providing a closed formula. We describe its symmetries, real-axis values, moment bounds and geometric interpretations. We use these to evaluate the mean ideal-tetrahedron volume directly from the density, recovering $\pi/6$, a recent theorem of Kabluchko and Schange. We then prove that the expected distance between two independently sampled hyperbolic geodesics in $\mathbb{H}^3$ is $4/3$, by evaluating the logarithmic potential of the cross-ratio distribution on the negative real axis. Further applications give the joint dihedral-angle density and an exact acute-tetrahedron probability, and a branched-cover probability law on the modular surface with exponentially small cusp tails.
item.dc:creator: Tim Marshall, Gaven Martin

item.title: Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the random velocity model with controlled sweeping
item.description: arXiv:2611.07694v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The present paper establishes the Richardson dispersion law, predicting the particle separation with time according to $\E R_t^2 \sim t^3$, as well as anomalous dissipation for the associated tracer, for a random H\"older continuous velocity vectorfield with controlled sweeping.
item.dc:creator: Charles Fefferman, Svitlana Mayboroda

item.title: Darboux transformations of linear birth-death processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.07974v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a previous paper we characterized the lower-upper (LU) and upper-lower (UL) factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth-death process whose Darboux transformations are again generators of birth-death processes. Here we apply these results to several classical models with linear rates and explicitly known spectral measures: the $M/M/\infty$ queue (Charlier polynomials), the linear birth-death processes (Meixner and Laguerre polynomials), and the linear models of Ismail, Letessier and Valent (associated Laguerre polynomials). For each of them we compute the factors in closed form, determine the admissible ranges of the parameters, and describe the rates, spectral measures and orthogonal polynomials of the Darboux-transformed processes.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Arcia-Manoleskos, Manuel Dom\'inguez de la Iglesia

item.title: Exact regions for the symmetrized Blest coefficient
item.description: arXiv:2611.08026v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spearman's rho treats all ranks alike, yet in many comparisons of two rankings an agreement at the top matters more than one at the bottom. Blest's rank correlation builds this preference into Spearman's rho, and its symmetrized version $\eta$, introduced by Genest and Plante, does so without favoring either of the two rankings. How far can such a top-weighted coefficient stray from other rank correlations? We answer this question for Spearman's rho, Blomqvist's beta and Chatterjee's rank correlation $\xi$ by determining the exact set of values that $\eta$ and each of these coefficients can attain jointly. Given Spearman's rho, $\eta$ can differ from it by at most $27/128$, and the extreme values of $\eta$ are attained only when the two rankings agree perfectly on the top ranks and are completely reversed on the bottom ranks, or vice versa. Given Blomqvist's beta, $\eta$ obeys exactly the same sharp bounds as Spearman's rho. For Chatterjee's rank correlation, both boundary curves are explicit and are attained by copulas with densities. Here symmetrization has a surprising effect. Compared with Blest's original coefficient, $\eta$ has a narrower range at fixed Spearman's rho, but near independence a wider range at fixed Chatterjee's rank correlation, where $|\eta|$ can come close to $\sqrt{11\xi/5}$ while Blest's coefficient stays below $\sqrt{32\xi/15}$. The proofs combine explicit Kantorovich potentials from optimal transport with a convex relaxation that turns out to be exact.
item.dc:creator: Marcus Rockel

item.title: Sharp moderate deviations and uniform Berry--Esseen bounds for Hotelling's $T^2$-statistic via Stein's method
item.description: arXiv:2611.08074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathbf X_1,\ldots,\mathbf X_n$ be independent random vectors in $\mathbb R^d$ with common mean $\boldsymbol\mu_n$, where $d\ge2$ is a fixed integer. Let $\bar{\mathbf X}_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf X_i$ denote the sample mean and let \[ \widehat\Sigma_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (\mathbf X_i-\bar{\mathbf X}_n) (\mathbf X_i-\bar{\mathbf X}_n)^\top \] denote the sample covariance matrix. Assume that the average covariance matrix is positive definite and that $\widehat\Sigma_n$ is nonsingular almost surely. For testing $H_0:\boldsymbol\mu_n=\boldsymbol\mu_0$, the Hotelling statistic is \[ T^2_{H,n} =n(\bar{\mathbf X}_n-\boldsymbol\mu_0)^\top \widehat\Sigma_n^{-1} (\bar{\mathbf X}_n-\boldsymbol\mu_0). \] Under $H_0$, we establish finite-sample Cram\'er-type moderate deviation results and uniform Berry--Esseen bounds under finite $p$th moments for $2<p\le3$. The moderate deviation error order is optimal over independent triangular arrays, as shown by explicit constructions. For identically distributed observations with a fixed distribution, we obtain \[ \sup_{0\le x\le b_n} \left| \frac{\mathbb P(T^2_{H,n}\ge x^2)} {\mathbb P(\chi_d^2\ge x^2)}-1 \right| = O\!\left((1+b_n)^p n^{-(p-2)/2}\right) \] for every nonnegative sequence $b_n=o(n^{(p-2)/(2p)})$. The uniform Berry--Esseen bound is $O(n^{-(p-2)/2})$. The proof uses a radial Stein identity and a recursive error estimate. We apply the results to chi-squared calibration in simultaneous testing.
item.dc:creator: Song-Hao Liu, Qi-Man Shao, Hao Shi, Jing-Yu Xu

item.title: Fourier level inequalities on the discrete cube via complex hypercontractivity and Riesz transforms
item.description: arXiv:2611.08289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Eldan's level-$1{:}3$ inequality is a central tool in his second-order correlation inequalities for increasing Boolean functions. His proof is going to Gaussian space and uses an entropy estimate for second Hermite tensors. We give a direct proof on the discrete hypercube. For increasing real-valued functions $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, we prove $$ W_3[f,g]\ge -2W_1[f,g]\log\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(f)\mathrm{Var}(g)}}{W_1[f,g]}\right). $$ The proof combines complex hypercontractivity with the discrete Riesz transforms. We also give a short proof of a level-$1:d$ inequality obtained by Keller and Kindler. As an application, we recover Eldan's correlation inequality with a slight improvement. If $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ are increasing and $g$ is antipodal, then $$ \mathrm{Cov}(f,g)\ge \frac1{24}\,\frac{\sum_i\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\mathrm{Inf}_i[g]}{\sqrt{\log\!\left(4e\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(f)\mathrm{Var}(g)}/(\sum_i\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\mathrm{Inf}_i[g])\right)}}, $$ where the square-root logarithm cannot be improved as shown in the OR--majority example.
item.dc:creator: Fan Chang, Zhenyu Li, Guanghui Wang, Mingrui Wang

item.title: Low-Temperature Sampling via Equilibrium Disagreements
item.description: arXiv:2611.08416v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a new framework for sampling at low temperatures using Glauber dynamics. In this regime, the coexistence of competing modes (commonly referred to as phases) creates bottlenecks that can make worst-case mixing exponentially slow. The main new ingredient in our framework is to relate convergence within a phase to the geometry of disagreements between two independent configurations drawn from that phase. As applications of our approach, we consider three canonical models on random regular graphs that have been central to low-temperature sampling, and establish fast convergence from natural initialisations of Glauber dynamics for every fixed degree. We show: --- For the hard-core model on random bipartite $d$-regular graphs, Glauber dynamics initialised from either one-sided independent set mixes within the corresponding phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps throughout the non-uniqueness regime $\lambda>\lambda_c(d)$. --- For the random-cluster model on random $d$-regular graphs, for every real $q>2$, Glauber dynamics initialised from the all-in edge set mixes within the ordered phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps for all $\beta\geq \beta_c$. Similarly, Glauber dynamics initialised from the all-out edge set mixes within the disordered phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps for $\beta\leq \beta_c$. --- For the ferromagnetic Ising model on random $d$-regular graphs, Glauber dynamics initialised from all-plus or all-minus mixes within the corresponding phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps throughout the low-temperature regime $\beta>\beta_c(d)$. We also give an $n^{2+o(1)}$-time algorithm that combines phase samples into samples from the full distribution, avoiding in particular time-costly approximations of the corresponding partition functions to the target sampling accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Galanis, Daniel Stefankovic

item.title: Tusn\'ady's problem and online two-sample thinning
item.description: arXiv:2611.08455v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the sharp order of discrepancy in Tusn\'ady's problem in every fixed dimension $d\ge 2$. The largest combinatorial discrepancy of $N$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to axis-parallel boxes is $\Theta_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$, extending Wei's planar result and matching Nikolov's upper bound. More strongly, with high probability, this lower bound holds simultaneously for every subset obtained by deleting at most a sufficiently small fixed fraction of a uniform $N$-point sample. We apply this geometric estimate to online thinning of two independent samples of size $n$ from an unknown common distribution, where observations must be kept or discarded upon arrival. For every fixed dimension $k\ge 1$ and expected deletion budget $\rho n$, with $0<\rho<2$, we prove that the minimax expected prefix discrepancy over lower orthants is $\Theta_{k,\rho}((\log n)^{k+1/2})$. In dimension one, the optimal terminal discrepancy is instead $\Theta_\rho((\log\log n)^{3/2})$, giving a sharp separation between the prefix and terminal objectives. For $k\ge 2$, we obtain terminal bounds differing by a factor of $\log n$. The lower bounds are based on Gaussian small-ball estimates for box-incidence matrices, while the upper bounds use stationary Metropolis thinning and, in one dimension, a terminal cancellation procedure.
item.dc:creator: Yuhao Lei

item.title: Uniqueness of the critical and supercritical Liouville quantum gravity metrics
item.description: arXiv:2110.00177v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that for each ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in [1,25)$, there is a unique metric associated with Liouville quantum gravity (LQG) with matter central charge ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M}$. An earlier series of works by Ding-Dub\'edat-Dunlap-Falconet, Gwynne-Miller, and others showed that such a metric exists and is unique in the subcritical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$, which corresponds to coupling constant $\gamma \in (0,2)$. The critical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} = 1$ corresponds to $\gamma=2$ and the supercritical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in (1,25)$ corresponds to $\gamma \in \mathbb C$ with $|\gamma| = 2$. Our metric is constructed as the limit of an approximation procedure called Liouville first passage percolation, which was previously shown to be tight for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in [1,25)$ by Ding and Gwynne (2020). In this paper, we show that the subsequential limit is uniquely characterized by a natural list of axioms. This extends the characterization of the LQG metric proven by Gwynne and Miller (2019) for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$ to the full parameter range $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,25)$. Our argument is substantially different from the proof of the characterization of the LQG metric for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$. In particular, the core part of the argument is simpler and does not use confluence of geodesics.
item.dc:creator: Jian Ding, Ewain Gwynne

item.title: Scaling limit of the colored ASEP and stochastic six-vertex models
item.description: arXiv:2403.01341v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the colored asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) and stochastic six vertex (S6V) model with fully packed initial conditions; the states of these models can be encoded by 2-parameter height functions. We show under Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling of time, space, and fluctuations that these height functions converge to the Airy sheet. Several corollaries follow. (1) For ASEP and the S6V model under the basic coupling, we consider the 4-parameter height function at position $y$ and time $t$ with a step initial condition at position $x$ and time $s < t$, and prove that under KPZ scaling it converges to the directed landscape. (2) As a consequence, in our paper arXiv:2412.18117, we prove that ASEPs and S6V models under the basic coupling, with multiple general initial data, converge to KPZ fixed points coupled through the directed landscape. (3) We prove that the colored ASEP stationary measures converge to the stationary horizon. (4) We prove a form of decoupling for the colored ASEP height functions, as well as for the stationary two-point function, as broadly predicted by the theory of non-linear fluctuating hydrodynamics. The starting point for our Airy sheet convergence result is an embedding of these colored models into a larger structure -- a color-indexed family of coupled line ensembles with an explicit Gibbs property, i.e., a colored Hall-Littlewood line ensemble. The core of our work then becomes to develop a framework to analyze the edge scaling limit of these ensembles.
item.dc:creator: Amol Aggarwal, Ivan Corwin, Milind Hegde

item.title: Inverting the operation of conditioning a branching process on extinction
item.description: arXiv:2411.06301v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is well-known that conditioning a supercritical (multi-type) branching process on the event that it eventually becomes extinct yields a subcritical branching process. We study the corresponding inverse problem: given a subcritical branching process, does there exist a supercritical branching process with the property that when we condition it on extinction, we get back the original subcritical branching process? We show that such a supercritical branching process (which we call a conjugate branching process) exists under mild hypotheses on the original subcritical branching process. We also show by example that if there are at least two types, then the conjugate branching process is not necessarily unique. Our results are relevant to the problem of constructing natural random planar maps whose scaling limit is given by supercritical Liouville quantum gravity. Moreover, conjugate branching processes can also be used to give alternative evolutionary hypotheses in cancer modeling.
item.dc:creator: Ewain Gwynne, Jiaqi Liu

item.title: From multitype branching to multitype coalescents and back: Genealogies, duality and examples
item.description: arXiv:2501.00329v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish new connections between multitype $\Lambda$-coalescents and multitype continuous state branching processes (CSBPs) through duality with a $\Lambda-$Wright-Fisher frequency process, and a homeomorphism between the spaces of the two classes of processes. The approach relies on a sequential sampling procedure for the frequency process of multitype CSBPs and provides an interpretation of multitype $\Lambda-$coalescents as the local genealogies of multitype CSBPs which gives further insight into different approaches to generalise $\Lambda-$coalescents to the multitype setup. As an application of the homeomorphism, we introduce and discuss multitype Beta-coalescents as the local genealogy of multitype $\alpha$-stable branching processes.
item.dc:creator: Adri\'an Gonz\'alez Casanova, Noemi Kurt, Imanol Nu\~nez Morales, Jos\'e Luis P\'erez

item.title: Operator level soft edge to bulk transition in $\beta$-ensembles via canonical systems
item.description: arXiv:2502.10305v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The stochastic Airy and sine operators, which are respectively a random Sturm-Liouville operator and a random Dirac operator, characterize the soft edge and bulk scaling limits of $\beta$-ensembles. Dirac and Sturm-Liouville operators are distinct operator classes which can both be represented as canonical systems, which gives a unified framework for defining important properties, such as their spectral data. Seeing both as canonical systems, we prove that in a suitable high-energy scaling limit, the Airy operator converges to the sine operator. We prove this convergence in the vague topology of canonical systems' coefficient matrices, and deduce the convergence of the associated Weyl-Titchmarsh functions and spectral measures. Our proof relies on a coupling between the Brownian paths that drive the two operators, under which the convergence holds in probability. This extends the corresponding result at the level of the eigenvalue point processes, proven by Valk\'o and Vir\'ag (2009) by comparison to the Gaussian $\beta$-ensemble.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Painchaud, Elliot Paquette

item.title: Averaging principle for rough slow-fast systems of level 3
item.description: arXiv:2504.03110v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The averaging principle for slow-fast systems of various kind of stochastic (partial) differential equations has been extensively studied. An analogous result was shown for slow-fast systems of rough differential equations driven by random rough paths a few years ago and the study of ``rough slow-fast systems" seems to be gaining momentum now. In all known results, however, the driving rough paths are of level 2. In this paper we formulate rough slow-fast systems driven by random rough paths of level 3 and prove the strong averaging principle of Khas'minskii-type.
item.dc:creator: Yuzuru Inahama

item.title: Heavy repulsion of clusters in Bernoulli percolation
item.description: arXiv:2509.10631v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider Bernoulli$(p)$ percolation on (non)unimodular quasi-transitive graphs and prove that, almost surely, for any two clusters $C$ and $C'$, the set of vertices in $C$ within distance one of $C'$ is light, i.e.\ it has finite total modular weight. This is a significant step towards resolving a longstanding question of H\"aggstr\"om, Peres, and Schonmann, and a generalization of a theorem of Tim\'ar, who proved the same result in the unimodular setting. We present two proofs. The first one is a hyperfiniteness argument that is specific to Bernoulli$(p)$ percolation and is new even in the unimodular case; the second is more general and follows Tim\'ar's approach, but requires the development of weighted analogues of several classical unimodular results. The new insight in both proofs is nonhyperfiniteness, which we obtain from the recently developed theory of measure class preserving equivalence relations and graphs. In particular, along the way we establish a generalization of a theorem of Benjamini, Lyons, and Schramm on the existence of an invariant random subgraph with positive weighted Cheeger constant, which is of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Sasha Bell, Tasmin Chu, Owen Rodgers, Grigory Terlov, Anush Tserunyan

item.title: Parisi formula and large deviations for mean-field spin glasses with Mattis interactions
item.description: arXiv:2603.12033v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider convex mean-field vector spin glasses perturbed by a general Mattis interaction $N G(m_N)$, where $m_N$ is a bounded vector-valued empirical average and $G$ is continuous. We prove a Parisi-type variational formula for the limiting quenched free energy and a quenched large deviation principle for $m_N$, both at every temperature. The approach is simple and modular: the only model-specific spin-glass input is the variational formula for every linear tilt of $m_N$ together with differentiability of the resulting free energy. The classical G\"artner--Ellis, Varadhan, and Bryc transfers then treat an arbitrary continuous $G$. Thus the same argument applies to a broad class of empirical observables and Mattis potentials, without a separate constrained-free-energy calculation for each model. As a scalar specialization, the framework contains the Gaussian spin-glass surrogate used in mismatched rank-one matrix estimation.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Bin Chen, Victor Issa

item.title: High-temperature free energy for non-convex mean-field spin glasses with Mattis interactions
item.description: arXiv:2603.12034v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study enriched mean-field vector spin glasses whose covariance function need not be convex. In a quantitative short-time regime, corresponding to sufficiently high temperature in the usual physical parameterization, we prove convergence of the quenched free energy to the differentiable solution of a infinite-dimensional Hamilton--Jacobi equation proposed for non-convex models. We identify that solution through its characteristics and a unique fixed point. The argument does not assume replica symmetry. We then allow a general continuous Mattis interaction $N G(m_N)$, obtain the corresponding variational formula, and prove a quenched large deviation principle for $m_N$. As an explicit application, we treat a bipartite model with Mattis fields, which is closely related to the Restricted Boltzmann Machine. The application requires neither a replica-symmetry assumption nor ellipticity or Nishimori identities; its restriction is the same quantitative high-temperature condition as in the general theorem.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Bin Chen, Victor Issa

item.title: The inradius law for the cavities of planar Brownian motion, with applications to the Wiener sausage
item.description: arXiv:2606.11248v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K_1=B[0,1]$ be the trace of a planar Brownian motion, and let $N_{\mathrm{in}}(\eta)$ count the bounded components of $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus K_1$ with inradius greater than $\eta$. As $\eta\downarrow0$, we prove that $\eta^2(\log(1/\eta))^2N_{\mathrm{in}}(\eta)\to c_{\mathrm{in}}=(\pi/2)\int G^2d\mathcal{L}\in(0,1/2]$ almost surely and in $L^p$ for every $p\in[1,2]$, where $G$ is the inradius divided by the square root of the area and $\mathcal{L}$ is Werner's limiting shape law. Inradius determines survival under thickening: a cavity contains a hole of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ if and only if its inradius exceeds $r$. Brownian scaling shows that, for fixed $r>0$ as $T\to\infty$, the number of cavities of $B[0,T]$ with inradius greater than $r$ is asymptotic to $4c_{\mathrm{in}}T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ in probability and in $L^p$, $p\in[1,2]$. It also gives lower bounds for the sausage's hole count, the Betti curve of its degree-one persistent homology, and its radius integrals, with constant $4c_{\mathrm{in}}$ in expectation and any smaller constant with probability tending to one. A matching upper bound cannot follow from general bounds in terms of perimeter, area, diameter or length. We prove that it is equivalent to a first-moment estimate for near-critical pockets: holes at level $\eta$ on which the distance to the trace is at most $2\eta$. Equivalently, it suffices to control residual pockets beyond one per cavity with inradius in $(\eta,2\eta]$. This estimate is proved in a companion paper, yielding the exact order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ for the expected number of holes.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Guillaume (CY Cergy Paris University)

item.title: Absolute Continuity of Monotone Aggregations under Positive Regression Dependence
item.description: arXiv:2606.21042v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we provide sufficient conditions for the absolute continuity of one-dimensional push-forwards of dependent random vectors. Suppose that $X$ has an absolutely continuous distribution and that the conditional distribution of an $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued random vector $Y$ given $X=x$ is nondecreasing in $x\in \mathbb{R}$ in the usual stochastic order. For Borel maps $g\colon \mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying a coordinatewise monotonicity condition in $Y$ and a uniform lower-increment condition in $X$, we prove that $g(X,Y)$ has an absolutely continuous distribution. The result requires neither independence nor a joint density, and allows the marginal law of $Y$ to be completely arbitrary. Moreover, the result remains valid if $\mathbb{R}^d$ is replaced by an arbitrary measurable space endowed with a reflexive binary relation. We discuss consequences for monotone risk aggregation and extensions of the familiar regularization by convolution beyond independent random variables.
item.dc:creator: Ben Goldys, Max Nendel

item.title: A Topological Formula for Potts Lattice Gauge Theory Correlations
item.description: arXiv:2607.02434v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We exhibit a formula relating the correlation between Wilson loop variables in Potts lattice gauge theory to a topological quantity in the plaquette random cluster model. As applications we prove exponential decay of correlations between slowly growing Wilson loop variables for Ising lattice gauge theory on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ at all but the critical temperature, we demonstrate that the correlation length is finite at sufficiently high or low temperatures in any dimension, and we show that the correlation length of the model on $\mathbb{Z}^4$ with free boundary conditions equals that of the dual model with constant boundary conditions when $q$ is prime.
item.dc:creator: Paul Duncan, Benjamin Schweinhart

item.title: Curvature-Dependent Path Concentration in Stochastic Fast-Slow Systems with Noise on the Slow Variable
item.description: arXiv:2607.16217v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study stochastic fast-slow systems with noise acting exclusively on the slow variable near uniformly attracting, normally hyperbolic critical manifolds $x=X^\ast(y)$. The deviation equation contains transmitted diffusion and an It\^o curvature forcing of order $O(\sigma^2\lVert D^2X^\ast\rVert)$. Using a parameter-dependent Lyapunov function and stopped martingale estimates, we obtain geometry-dependent concentration bounds under the sufficient noise restriction $\sigma\le C_0\min(\sqrt{\varepsilon},\varepsilon^{1/4}L_{\mathrm{geom}}/\sqrt{\lambda_0})$, where $\lambda_0$ is the uniform spectral gap and $L_{\mathrm{geom}}=\sqrt{\lambda_0/(\lVert D^2X^\ast\rVert\lVert h\rVert^2)}$. For fixed geometry and any fixed $p>0$, the confidence radius on $[0,T/\varepsilon]$ is $O(\varepsilon+\sigma^2+\sigma\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)})$, with stopped fast-variable failure probability at most $\varepsilon^p$; slow-variable exit is controlled separately. We also establish an adiabatic error bound of order $O(\varepsilon+\sigma\sqrt{\varepsilon}+\sigma^2\lVert D^2X^\ast\rVert)$, with explicit failure probabilities. These estimates quantify the curvature dependence of fast-variable concentration and its $O(\varepsilon)$ contribution to the slow-error upper bound for fixed geometry.
item.dc:creator: Yefan Wu

item.title: Stable and Gaussian Fluctuation Limit of a L\'evy-Driven Slow-Fast System
item.description: arXiv:2609.09906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study fluctuation limit of a slow-fast system driven by $\alpha$-stable L\'evy noise with $1<\alpha<2.$ The slow component is generated by an odd polynomial function $f(y):=y^q,$ while in the fast component, the drift is $g(y):=-|y|^p\operatorname{sgn}(y)$ for some $p>0.$ Although the noise is given, the fluctuation limit is either a stable process or a Brownian motion, depending on both $p$ and $\alpha.$ The critical line between stable limit and Brownian limit is $q+1-p=\alpha/2.$
item.dc:creator: Qingming Zhao, Xueru Liu, Wei Wang

item.title: Third-moment cancellation and predictable representation in finite-state BSDE approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20880v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study finite-state approximations of Brownian-driven Markovian backward stochastic differential equations when the same one-step increment is used both for weak propagation and for martingale representation. For a centered isotropic state-independent increment with vanishing third moment, we prove first-order convergence of the Markov value field, its spatial gradient, and the predictable $Z$-field under suitable smoothness assumptions. The corresponding orthogonal martingale has maximal $L^2$ size $O(h^{1/2})$. We identify its quadratic representation defect and prove a joint functional limit theorem for the state process and the normalized orthogonal martingale, which in particular yields a mixed-normal terminal limit with path-dependent conditional variance. On the trace-free quadratic sector, the representation defect has the sharp universal operator lower bound $d/[2(d+2)]$; equality holds exactly for normalized laws that are weighted spherical 4-designs. In dimension $d\geq 2$, vanishing third moment is incompatible with exact scalar one-step predictable representation for any finite-state centered isotropic increment. Consequently, every such exact-representation law has a nonzero cubic direction, and a smooth Fourier terminal condition converts this direction into a sharp global $h^{1/2}$ weak error. For the centrally symmetric regular-simplex rule we also identify the leading quadratic GKW component, compute the exact first-order asymptotic of the accumulated orthogonal-martingale variance, and recover it from the general functional limit. Thus the same third-order tensor links weak accuracy and predictable representation, yielding an accuracy-representation tradeoff for finite-state BSDE approximations.
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Tanaka

item.title: Gaussian Matrices and Exterior Forms: Deterministic Principal Ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.03495v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For an infinite Gaussian matrix with independent entries and doubly monotone variances, we identify its algebraic principal ideal by a deterministic shell profile. The exact boundedness condition also implies compactness. A lower singular-value estimate uniform in the mean gives an exact sum law under each fixed compact perturbation. Conditional products and spatial compression yield the corresponding classification for Gaussian evaluations of Hilbert two-forms. For Wiener area of covariance rank at least two, the generator is the covariance tail divided by its index. The area and covariance generate the same ideal precisely under regularity at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Guangqian Zhao

item.title: Quantum Adiabatic Theorem under Wiener Noise: Maximal Mean-Square Estimates
item.description: arXiv:2611.06029v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive maximal mean-square adiabatic estimates for finite-dimensional stochastic Schr\"odinger equations with Hamiltonian-proportional Wiener noise. For deterministic $C^2$ Hamiltonians whose eigenvalues have constant multiplicities and do not cross on $[0,1]$, we construct a unitary stochastic adiabatic intertwiner driven by the same Wiener process as the exact propagator. A commutator argument, It\^o calculus, and Doob's maximal inequality yield an explicit bound for the expected supremum of their squared operator-norm difference on a selected initial eigenspace. Under uniform coefficient bounds, the physical noise scaling $\alpha=\sigma T^{-\gamma}$, where $T$ is the total evolution time and $\sigma\geq0$ and $\gamma\geq0$ are fixed, gives maximal mean-square error $O(T^{-2}+\sigma^4T^{-4\gamma}+\sigma^2T^{-(2\gamma+1)})$. Consequently, adiabatic convergence holds for every $\gamma>0$ as $T\to\infty$, while $\gamma\geq1/2$ recovers the deterministic $O(T^{-1})$ bound for the root-mean-square maximal error. For fixed nonzero physical noise amplitude, the estimate leaves convergence unresolved.
item.dc:creator: A. M. H. H. Caldera, R. P. K. De Silva, K. K. W. A. S. Kumara, B. P. W. Fernando

item.title: Nonlinear PDEs with modulated dispersion II: Korteweg-de Vries equation
item.description: arXiv:1406.7675v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: (Due to the limit on the number of characters for an abstract set by arXiv, the full abstract can not be displayed here. See the abstract in the paper.) We study dispersive equations with a time non-homogeneous modulation acting on the linear dispersion term. As primary models, we consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) and related equations such as the Benjamin-Ono equation (BO) and the intermediate long wave equation (ILW), imposing certain irregularity conditions on the time non-homogeneous modulation. In this work, we establish phenomena called regularization by noise in three-folds: (i) When the modulation is sufficiently irregular, we show that the modulated KdV on both the circle and the real line is locally well-posed in the regime where the (unmodulated) KdV equation is known to be ill-posed. In particular, given any $s \in \mathbb R$, we show that the modulated KdV on the circle with a sufficiently irregular modulation is locally well-posed in $H^s(\mathbb T)$. Moreover, by adapting the $I$-method to the current modulated setting, we prove global well-posedness of the modulated KdV in negative Sobolev spaces. (ii) It is known that certain (semilinear) dispersive equations such as BO and ILW exhibit quasilinear nature. We show that sufficiently irregular modulations make the modulated versions of these equations semilinear by establishing their local well-posedness by a contraction argument, providing local Lipschitz continuity of the solution map. (iii) We also prove nonlinear smoothing for these modulated equations, where we show that a gain of regularity of the nonlinear part becomes (arbitrarily) larger for more irregular modulations. As applications of our approach, we also include further examples.
item.dc:creator: Khalil Chouk, Massimiliano Gubinelli, Guopeng Li, Jiawei Li, Tadahiro Oh

item.title: Functional relations for higher-order free cumulants
item.description: arXiv:2112.12184v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish the functional relations between generating series of higher-order free cumulants and moments in higher-order free probability, solving an open problem posed fifteen years ago by Collins, Mingo, \'Sniady and Speicher. We propose an extension of free probability theory, which governs the all-order topological expansion in unitarily invariant matrix ensembles, with a corresponding notion of free cumulants and give as well their relation to moments via functional relations. Our approach is based on the study of a master transformation involving double monotone Hurwitz numbers via semi-infinite wedge techniques, building on the recent advances of the last-named author with Bychkov, Dunin-Barkowski and Kazarian. We illustrate our formulas by computing the first few decaying terms of the correlation functions of an ensemble of spiked GUE matrices, going beyond the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem.
item.dc:creator: Ga\"etan Borot, S\'everin Charbonnier, Elba Garcia-Failde, Felix Leid, Sergey Shadrin

item.title: Mirror Descent-Ascent for mean-field min-max problems
item.description: arXiv:2402.08106v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study two variants of the mirror descent-ascent (MDA) algorithm for solving min-max problems on the space of measures: simultaneous and alternating. We work under assumptions of convexity-concavity and relative smoothness of the payoff function with respect to a suitable Bregman divergence, defined on the space of measures via flat derivatives. We establish non-asymptotic convergence rates to mixed Nash equilibria, measured in the Nikaid\^{o}-Isoda error, proving an $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1/2})$ rate for simultaneous MDA and an improved $\mathcal{O}(N^{-2/3})$ rate for alternating MDA. The main technical contribution is an infinite-dimensional dual space analysis that relates Bregman divergences on measures to dual Bregman divergences on spaces of bounded continuous functions, allowing us to control asymmetric commutator terms created by alternating updates. The results substantially generalize prior analyses restricted to bilinear objectives and also apply to nonlinear convex-concave problems on measure spaces, thereby providing a unified theoretical foundation for MDA in mean-field min-max optimization.
item.dc:creator: Razvan-Andrei Lascu, Mateusz B. Majka, {\L}ukasz Szpruch

item.title: Q-Learning under Finite Model Uncertainty
item.description: arXiv:2407.04259v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a robust Q-learning algorithm for Markov decision processes under model uncertainty when each state--action pair is associated with a finite ambiguity set of candidate transition kernels. This finite-measure framework enables user-designed uncertainty models, including competing fitted models and stress scenarios. {The learner observes successor states and their deterministic rewards from every candidate simulator, without requiring explicit knowledge of the transition probabilities or the reward function.} We establish almost sure convergence of the learned Q-function to the robust optimum, and derive a time-uniform high-probability error certificate that separates an observable empirical Bellman residual from transition-kernel estimation error. We also give quantitative finite-ambiguity approximation results for Wasserstein and parametric uncertainty models on finite state spaces. Numerical examples illustrate the effect of scenario selection and compare the tabular algorithm with robust value iteration.
item.dc:creator: Julian Sester, C\'ecile Decker

item.title: Langevin Monte-Carlo Provably Learns Depth Two Neural Nets at Any Size and Data
item.description: arXiv:2503.10428v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this note we prove that the Langevin Monte Carlo (LMC) algorithm can minimize the population risk of appropriately regularized depth-2 nets with no restrictions on the size of the net and for any choice of training data --- and we give non-asymptotic convergence rates for it. We achieve this via showing that in q-Renyi divergence, the iterates of LMC converge to the Gibbs distribution of certain Frobenius norm regularized losses for these nets --- in both classification and regression settings. The key technicality of the work is two-fold (a) to keep the amount of regularization needed be independent of the size of the net and (b) to obtain convergence rates that scale with just the Poincare constant of the corresponding Gibbs measure. This work synthesizes several recent observations about isoperimetry conditions under which LMC converges and that two-layer neural loss functions can always be regularized by a constant amount such that they satisfy the Villani conditions, and thus their Gibbs measures satisfy a Poincare inequality.
item.dc:creator: Dibyakanti Kumar, Samyak Jha, Anirbit Mukherjee

item.title: Stochastic Derivative Estimation for Discontinuous Sample Performances: A Leibniz Integration Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2511.00006v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Based on the multidimensional Leibniz integral rule, we propose a novel unbiased stochastic derivative estimation framework for sample performance functions that are discontinuous in the parameter of interest. In this framework, for general discontinuities, a change of variables followed by the Leibniz integral rule generally yields a multi-run estimator, whereas for indicator-type discontinuities, a suitable transformation of the sample performance leads directly to a single-run estimator. The new framework includes existing likelihood ratio (LR)-based approaches as special cases and applies more broadly. In particular, it encompasses generalized LR (GLR) methods and the new formulation permits us to obtain much milder and simpler sufficient regularity conditions for these estimators to be unbiased, compared with the conditions given in previous papers. We also provide guidance on how to construct efficient single-run estimators in settings where existing methods may require the simulation of multiple sample paths or may be inapplicable. We validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework through an inventory-price control problem.
item.dc:creator: Xingyu Ren, Michael C. Fu, Pierre L'Ecuyer

item.title: Propagation of chaos for the Landau equation via microcanonical binary collisions
item.description: arXiv:2511.09035v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a fully constructive, conservative, and collision-level realization of Kac's program for the spatially homogeneous Landau equation across the full interaction range, including the Coulomb case. Our model is the microcanonical binary-collision (MBC) process: a reversible pure-jump $N$-particle Markov process, realizing the grazing-collision mechanism via small conservative rotations of relative velocities. Under suitable assumptions on the initial data, we prove propagation of chaos in the joint mean-field and grazing-collision limit ($N\to\infty, h\to0$), identifying any limit point with the unique solution in the relevant weak-solution class. The empirical measures converge in quadratic Wasserstein distance, while fixed-order marginals converge strongly in $L^1$ at every fixed time. Furthermore, we rigorously derive the Landau master equation as the fixed-$N$ grazing-collision limit of the MBC process. The proof combines Fisher-information dissipation, compactness, and uniqueness; for $\gamma\in[-3,-2)$, second-order information along collision directions yields the time-integrable $L^\infty$ bound needed for uniqueness.
item.dc:creator: Kai Du

item.title: A Generalized Framework for Singular Fractional Burgers Equations with Stochastic Forcing
item.description: arXiv:2602.07492v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the regularization effect of fractional stochastic forcing on Burgers-type equations with fractional dissipation, with an application to the Degasperis--Procesi (DP) equation. In particular, we consider the perturbation induced by the singular noise $|D|^{1/2}\xi$ and establish local well-posedness in the negative Sobolev space $H^{-1/4+\delta}$ for some small $\delta>0$. Due to the singular nature of the nonlinear interactions, classical solution theories cannot be directly applied. Inspired by the framework developed in \cite{hairer2013solving,gubinelli2017kpz}, we introduce a generalized solution theory based on an enhanced structure and derive the effective equations satisfied by these generalized solutions. Our main contribution is the establishment of a general framework for describing singular PDEs driven by rough data. Moreover, we prove the convergence of the associated non-Gaussian rough structures in the fractional dissipation setting. As an application, we apply this framework to the stochastic Degasperis--Procesi equation and obtain its local well-posedness in the low-regularity regime.
item.dc:creator: Shuolin Zhang, Zhaonan Luo, Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: Second-order PACF asymptotics and discrimination between fractional Gaussian noise and $\FARIMA(0,d,0)$
item.description: arXiv:2605.31416v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fractional Gaussian noise and $\FARIMA(0,d,0)$ have the same long-memory pole $|\theta|^{-2d}$ and hence the same leading PACF law $\alpha(n)\sim d/n$. We show that this agreement breaks at the first non-universal order. For $0<d<1/2$, the pure fGn PACF satisfies $$ \alpha_{\fGn}(n)=\frac d n+\frac{C_{\fGn}(d)}{n^2}+o(n^{-2}), \qquad C_{\fGn}(d)<d^2, $$ The proof uses the Bingham--Inoue--Kasahara representation, a phase-coefficient expansion for fGn, and a Hankel-operator perturbation argument. Thus the fGn spectral envelope is invisible at first order but visible in second-order finite prediction, explaining why short-memory order selection can differ when fGn data are fitted by FARIMA-type models.
item.dc:creator: Chunhao Cai

item.title: Graph-theoretic framework for semi-Markov networks: transient and stationary occupation probabilities, hitting times and weak ergodicity breaking
item.description: arXiv:2610.13505v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that finite semi-Markov networks admit explicit combinatorial representations of their Laplace-transformed occupation probabilities and hitting-time distributions as sums over weighted spanning trees and forests of an augmented graph, generalizing the previously developed graph-theoretic framework for Markov networks. These representations yield asymptotic results, including the long-time scaling of hitting-time survival probabilities in the presence of infinite-mean sojourn times. They also extend recently derived combinatorial formulas for hitting-time moments to the semi-Markov setting, where non-Markovian corrections appear in higher moments. For finite-mean sojourn times, the framework recovers the known stationary distribution through a generalization of the Markov Chain Tree Theorem, with transition rates replaced by pseudo-rates. In particular, the mean hitting-time formula coincides with that of a Markov network with the corresponding pseudo-rates, which also yields a short graph-theoretic proof of the previously established constancy of Kemeny's constant for finite-mean semi-Markov networks. Finally, we use the same framework to extend established results on weak ergodicity breaking for time-additive state observables that are nonconstant on the support of the limiting distribution in heavy-tailed semi-Markov networks, allowing for generally heterogeneous, transition-dependent waiting-time distributions.
item.dc:creator: Julian Voits

item.title: Subgaussian Vector Balancing by an Ising Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.18639v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the guaranties of the Gram-Schmidt Walk Algorithm of Bansal, Dadush, Garg, and Lovett can be achieved by an Ising model. Given vectors $v_1, \ldots, v_n$ of norm less than 1, we give a closed form for a centrally symmetric distribution on a vector $\sigma \in \{\pm 1 \}^n$ so that the signed sum $\sum_j \sigma(j) v_j$ is $1$-subgaussian. We show that the Glauber dynamics for this model mix rapidly provided that the norms of the input vectors are bounded below 1 by an inverse-polynomial. The proofs employ the theory of Lorentzian polynomials, and we use these techniques to show fast mixing bounds for other spin systems.
item.dc:creator: Heng Guo, Daniel A. Spielman, Xinyuan Zhang
